verdict.rationale: CodeRabbit's docs say developers can challenge recommendations in chat, and that review preferences learned from those conversations are applied automatically to future reviews. That directly covers pushing back and having the feedback stick. A community reply only hedges that it 'supposedly' remembers, which is skepticism rather than a concrete counter-example. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on confirmation that rejected feedback actually stops recurring, and documentation on how learnings are scoped, viewed or edited.

support.subject: As a developer, I can push back on a bad review comment and the reviewer learns — it stops repeating the same rejected feedback

citations.quote: you can ask follow-up questions, request clarifications, challenge recommendations, or explore alternative approaches
